name: Discovery Tension Rules
description: Configuration for preserving unresolved tensions as part of human complexity.
principles: Preserve tensions rather than resolve them.
Do not categorize tensions into fixed types.
Do not treat tension as inconsistency or failure.
Treat competing desires as meaningful evidence of human complexity.
Keep both sides of a tension visible when both are supported by participant statements.
discoverySignals: The participant expresses two desires that pull in different directions.
The participant values one thing but repeatedly chooses another due to context.
The participant names a frustration connected to something they also want.
The participant describes different versions of themselves in different environments.
The participant shows hesitation, qualification, or ambivalence around an important area.
handlingGuidance: Ask exploratory questions that help understand both sides.
Record the tension without declaring a winner.
Attach evidence to each side when available.
Avoid recommendations until understanding is sufficient.
Use tension as a signal for deeper discovery, not as a problem to solve.
